title: Widen the settled-rule regexes for timestamp writers and directory listing (O-031)
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: FAIL W01 fires the timestamp rule, 0 hit(s): File.SetAttributes(path, FileAttributes.Normal); ... FAIL L02 fires the listing rule, 0 hit(s): var subs = dir.GetDirectories(); — 7 check(s) failed.

Rule 2 ('only the directory-listing open path may write a file-system timestamp', .taad/fitness.yaml:746-764) matches File.SetAttributes in src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.cs outside its excepted files: missing
Rule 4 ('only DirectoryReader lists a directory', .taad/fitness.yaml:774-791) matches the DirectoryInfo instance listings GetFiles(...) and GetDirectories(...): missing
A second, unfenced timestamp/attribute writer or directory listing in Core outside the one sanctioned call site fails a settled rule (no settled rule stays green on it): missing

Scope: spike 1's union (rule 2 at 11 patterns, rule 4 at 7, a new entry, 21 plant rows) against the R2-m4 two-line minimum, which alone closes the repro (spike 2). The practice designer raised over_engineering_flag against their own union. The trimmed version keeps `\bFile\.SetAttributes\b`, GetFiles|GetDirectories in the instance pattern, the because-text fix and rows S58, S64 and S65, and drops everything else.

Placement of the new entry: the engine appends it at the end of the file under '# settled by SL-104' (this design), or it is hand-inserted after rule 4 so the three sibling fences read together (the proposal). Only the first marker matters to any tool.

The Attributes setter in a separate entry that excepts DirectoryReader.cs, against a narrower right-hand-side pattern (one that requires FileAttributes) inside rule 2. The narrower pattern misses `fi.Attributes = attrs;`.
Rewriting the because-texts to list what is fenced and what escapes, against simply deleting the 'every way' sentence.

The untracked .taad-scratch/ (about 95 planted Planted*.cs files, copies of fitness.yaml and probe scripts) came from the repro and investigation stages and was left in place; remove it or ignore it before the slice merges, since git status shows it as untracked.
Rules 2 and 4 and the Attributes entry still have no xUnit twin, so dotnet test stays green when they break; only the Fitness check and the harness enforce them (design filed_for_later).

Residual spellings a text rule cannot see are pinned as residual corpus rows and named in the because-texts: object initializers of Attributes and times, reflection, a delegate from a using-static method group, and Encrypt/Decrypt through using static. Closing them needs a symbol-based or AST check.
Content writes and moves that change times as a side effect (File.Write*, Move, Copy, Replace, SetAccessControl) are outside rule 2's family and remain a separate design decision.

The corpus runner's live census check fails for any new Set*/set_*/Encrypt/Decrypt/listing member on .NET 10, so it can go red on a future runtime that adds one; that red is intended, and the fix is to add the member to the census.

deviation: The design pinned 21 plant rows (S58-S78) and a _note count of 144; the accepted M1 and M2 findings required one fire row each, so there are 25 (S79 += on a time, S80 -= on Attributes, S81 |= on IsReadOnly, S82 FileInfo.Encrypt()), 148 rows in plants.json and 161 in the all scenario.

deviation: The design said Encrypt/Decrypt is '\bFile\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b'; per accepted M2 it is the receiver-free '\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b' (still one pattern, so 11 and 7 hold). The time, IsReadOnly and Attributes patterns carry the M1 operator classes and (?![=>]).

deviation: The design said the acceptance repro is the only new test; the CLOSE-THE-CLASS obligations O-017 and O-018 required a committed corpus, so two files were added (the corpus JSON and its runner). The repro itself is committed unchanged.

deviation: The design asked for a build-time GetMethods() enumeration treated as 'a missing pattern, not a residual'; per accepted M3 the enumeration was run once and pinned as the census in the corpus, with out-of-family members (UnixFileMode, SetCurrentDirectory) and residuals named, and the runner re-checks it on .NET 10.

deviation: The design's architecture_rules entry in design-slice-1.json still shows the pre-M1 pattern (?!=), although the finding says it is updated. I edited the engine-appended block in place instead, as accepted M4 describes. The engine's _append_rules appends only rules whose name it has not seen, so a re-run should not add a duplicate.

deviation: The design said to put the guard in one case; accepted M6 asked for it to be split. Only the C-013 key exists, so its command is RuleCases C-001 (the settled-count check), and C-002..C-005 were run separately and are listed under tests.
deviation: No known-outside-defect workaround applies: this slice fixes the project's own rules, so KnownWorkarounds and its settings are untouched.

drift: design-slice-1.json's architecture_rules entry still has the pre-M1 pattern `(?m)\.Attributes\s*[|&^]?=(?!=)` and the old because-text, although the M4 disposition said the design entry would be updated. The tree has `[-+|&^]?=(?![=>])`. The builder declared this. It is harmless while the yaml block exists, because design.py:1179-1209 appends only unseen names. If the block were ever deleted, a redesign would re-append the stale pattern.

drift: Apart from what the builder declared (25 rows instead of 21, _note 148 instead of 144, receiver-free Encrypt, the corpus and its runner added, the census pinned, the guard case split to RuleCases C-001), I found no other departure from the design.
drift: Round 2 found no new departure from the design. The drift recorded in round 1 stands.
not reached: The engine's merge/commit-time gate (minorlane) was not run. I ran fitness.check through the MCP tool and the harness, not the gate itself.
not reached: My planted lines were matched as text and never compiled. The build's corpus compiled its own spellings. That matters for a text rule only if a quiet row would not compile in real code.
not reached: I did not run the whole xUnit suite. src is unchanged, and only the yaml-reading rule tests were run.
not reached: I did not re-run RuleCases C-002..C-005. The build ran them one at a time and they passed. I re-ran C-001 and rules-parity.

not reached: These spellings stay unfenced and are carried on the backlog, not checked here: deconstruction assignment and ++/-- on Attributes (SC-321), method groups through a using alias (SC-322), whitespace, comment or @ between the dot and the member (SC-323), object initializers, reflection, and delegates from using-static method groups.
not reached: Nothing in the default `dotnet test` run enforces rules 2 and 4 or the Attributes entry, because they have no xUnit twin. Only the Fitness check and the harness do.

critique missed: M1 widened the setter patterns to `[-+|&^]?=` for compound assignment but did not enumerate the other assignment forms of the same properties. Unary `fi.Attributes++` / `--` (enum) and deconstruction `(fi.LastWriteTime, fi.Attributes) = (...)` both compile and match no pattern. A check could ask, for each fenced property setter, which assignment forms C# permits (=, op=, ++/--, deconstruction, initializer).

critique missed: The design made only Encrypt/Decrypt receiver-free (via M2). `\bFile\.SetAttributes\b` and `\b(File|Directory)\.Set(LastAccess|LastWrite|Creation)Time` still need the literal type name, so a method group through `using F = System.IO.File;` (`F.SetAttributes`) escapes. The inconsistency was visible in the design, since rule 4's instance pattern was already receiver-free.

critique missed: No question was asked about what C# allows between the member-access dot and the member name: spaces, a newline, a /* */ comment (blanked to spaces by strip_comments) or an `@` verbatim identifier. Every dotted pattern in rule 2, rule 4 and the Attributes entry needs the name directly after `.`. Eight such lines compiled and fired no rule under Store/.

code-review missed: Round 1 compiled and probed alias and deconstruction spellings against the same diff but did not probe whitespace, newline or `@` between the dot and the member. Only the second 'attacker' round found it. Any round-1 review of a text rule should try token-level spacing variants of every dotted pattern.

critique missed: The M2 fix replaced `\bFile\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b` with the receiver-free `\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b` without running it against non-file receivers (RSA, other crypto types). It over-fences `rsa.Encrypt(...)`. The critique should have asked what other types in System.* expose Encrypt/Decrypt.

critique missed: The M4 disposition said the design's architecture_rules entry is updated to the M1 pattern. Only the design stage can write design-slice-1.json, so the build could not honour it, and the design record kept the pre-M1 pattern and because-text.

still unknown: Does anything re-run tests/bugs/SL-104-SettledRuleClassCorpus.Tests.ps1 after the slice merges? It is not in the default dotnet test run, and rules 2 and 4 and the Attributes entry have no xUnit twin. Only the Fitness check and the harness exercise them, so the 178-row corpus and its live .NET 10 census may be dead weight once the slice's own cases stop being measured.

still unknown: Does the engine's merge-time minorlane gate behave the same on the 92-rule yaml? Validate ran fitness.check through the MCP tool and the harness, not the gate itself, so this was not reached.

still unknown: Would model-answered dispositions survive a person's check? Ten findings (7 critique, 3 code review) were answered by a model and none was reviewed. Four spelling families were then waived on 'does not weigh a lap on its own'. It is unknown whether a person would have taken the zero-line pattern fixes in this slice.

went wrong: The slice shipped with its own class claim still false. The corpus says it bounds 'every spelling the compiler accepts', yet ++/-- on Attributes, deconstruction, a using-alias method group and whitespace/@ after the dot all compile and escape every pattern. All four were found only by code review, so the O-031 failure mode (a rule claiming more than it fences) survives in a narrower form. The five escape spellings from the earlier waivers are on the backlog as SC-321, SC-322 and SC-323.

went wrong: The design said the repro was the only new test and pinned 21 plant rows and a `_note` count of 144. The build delivered 25 rows, 148 in plants.json, and a 178-row corpus with a runner (9 files). All of it was declared, but the design's size claim was off by a whole test subsystem.

went wrong: Critique and code review each ran twice. Both first runs halted on findings waiting for disposition, and every disposition (7 critique, 3 code review) was model-answered and counted as untriaged. No person has checked any of them, so these gates' precision is still unmeasured.

went wrong: The critique's own fix for M2, the receiver-free `\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b`, over-fences non-file receivers. Validate found `rsa.Encrypt(...)` firing rule 2. The proposed regex was not run against a quiet-corpus before the build, and the 41 quiet corpus rows did not cover it.

went wrong: M4's disposition promised to update design-slice-1.json, which the build cannot do. The design record still carries the pre-M1 Attributes pattern and the old because-text. Harmless while the yaml block exists, but a stale pattern would come back if the block were ever deleted and the design re-run.

went wrong: Validate marked the acceptance repro (SL-104-SettledRuleSpellings.Tests.ps1) not-run, along with the whole xUnit suite, RuleCases C-002..C-005 and the minorlane merge gate. It substituted its own 46-case matrix, and the build and code review had run the repro. The acceptance command was discharged by the engine (O-001), but validate itself did not re-run it.

went wrong: The untracked .taad-scratch/ (about 95 Planted*.cs files, copies of fitness.yaml, probe scripts) from the repro and investigation stages was still in the worktree at build. The record does not show it removed before the slice ships.
